The *Mūlavāraniddesa* (Ya 1.2.1) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Yamaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. As its title indicates, it constitutes the full exposition (*niddesa*) of the section on roots (*mūlavāra*) within the *Mūlayamaka*, expanding the framework set out in the summary matrix (*Mūlavārauddesa*, Ya 1.1.1) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language, but does not provide an English title [SuttaCentral].
No curated cross-canonical parallels are recorded for the text in SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse, comprising 3,333 matching passages across 33 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest volumes of shared material occur with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (1,208 matches) and the *Mūlavārauddesa* (932 matches), reflecting the systematic expansion of identical analytical formulae [DharmaNexus]. The text is also heavily cited in and shared with the commentarial literature, including the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā*, and *Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā*, as well as other Yamaka chapters such as the *Paṇṇattivāraniddesa* (Ya 9.1.2) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus records phraseological matches with various sutta passages, such as the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), *Opamma Saṁyutta* (SN 20), *Sallekha Sutta* (MN 8), and *Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta* (MN 9), as well as the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 14.1) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments detected by DharmaNexus include Sanskrit matches with the *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra* and Tibetan matches with the *Yogācārabhūmau bodhisattvabhūmivyākhyā* (D4047) and the *Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅga-nirdeśa-sūtra* (D0211), representing machine-detected parallels in formulaic Abhidharma exposition rather than direct historical lineages [DharmaNexus].
